messages:
monitoring-bot: ALERT: gpu-node-109 gpu0 Xid spike detected (4 events in 12m). severity=warning

lina: FYI — same card has shown intermittent Xid spikes ~past 6h, node kept flapping between healthy/flaky. saw one k8s eviction yesterday. thinking we should try a soft-isolate + retry policy before full cordon/evict.

dave: can you paste the counts and which workloads were impacted?

lina: quick summary: xid counts per 10m: 0,1,0,3,2,5 (peak 5). one pod eviction (ml-train-prod) restarted job in slurm fallback which bumped queue time. no GPU ECC fatal logs yet.

ajay: soft-isolate sounds good but watch reserved capacity / reserved pools. if we soft-isolate and keep scheduling elsewhere we might blow out our dedicated capacity for dedicated customers. need priority-aware rules (slurm partitions vs k8s qos).

lee: propose a two-step automated flow:
1) soft-isolate: taint node with gpu-flaky=true:NoSchedule and set annotation gpu-flaky-since=<ts>, DO NOT evict running pods (no drain).
2) monitor for 20m window; if Xid persists (>=3 in 10m) then cordon + graceful drain with eviction policy that prefers preemptible/batch jobs first.

Example healthhook config I prototyped:
```yaml
healthhook:
  xid_spike:
    window: 10m
    threshold: 3
    initial_action: soft-isolate
    soft_isolate_taint: gpu-flaky=true:NoSchedule
    retry_window: 20m
    escalate_action: cordon-and-evict
    max_attempts: 2
```

lina: this matches what I had in mind. key is "soft" step to avoid unnecessary evictions for noisy cards. also add a cooldown to re-admit node if stable (auto-untain after 1h).

ops-oncall: I can run a canary tomorrow 10:00 PST. will pick a non-prod pool and simulate spikes (nvidia-smi -l 60 with crafted workload). need PR + feature-flag gate first.

sre-bot: CI check: healthhook schema lint OK. no merge conflicts with main.

toni: we should also tie in HVAC/thermal telemetry and ECC-corrected counters. if ECC corrected > 100 across 3 checks => mark for replacement. that's the only time we do auto-replace; otherwise prefer soft handling. note: replacement triggers hardware ticket + cost impact (~$2k/node RMA).

dave: how do we avoid thrashing between regions? us-east has lower spare capacity than us-west. can we limit auto-escalate to region tags?

lee: yes, add region whitelist to the hook. default to {us-west1, eu-west1} for rollback 1.

ajay: also add a quota check before taint: if available spare GPUs < 5% we should skip auto-isolate and escalate to paging SRE (no automated eviction).

lina: action items:
- @lee open PR adding xid_spike hook + region whitelist + quota gate (PR #1248)
- @ops-oncall run canary in non-prod (tomorrow 10:00 PST)
- @toni add ECC-corrected -> replacement rule to playbook
- @ajay/ops define reserved-capacity threshold to skip auto-isolate

ajay: +1

ops-oncall: noted, will coordinate and post results in this thread.

lina: I'll draft the rollout plan: feature-flagged in configmap, roll to us-west1 canary, watch latency/cost dashboards (batch spillover), then expand to eu-west1. rollback = flip feature-flag off.

monitoring-bot: NOTE: scheduled canary window for 1798590720 - 1798594320 (tomorrow 10:00 PST) created.

lina: thanks all. I'll add the playbook link + test checklist to the PR. :thumbsup:
